issues.legal_issue: An executing court’s order refusing to inquire into a third party’s execution claim for want of jurisdiction, without deciding the claim on its merits, is not an adjudication treated as a decree.
material_facts: Third parties claiming an independent right and title to the property applied after being dispossessed in execution, seeking adjudication of their claim and restoration of possession.
The executing court refused to inquire into the claim, reasoning that it had become functus officio after the decree had been executed, and did not decide the applicants’ rights on the merits.
The High Court treated the executing court’s refusal as a deemed decree and dismissed the applicants’ supervisory challenge on the ground that an appeal was available.
issues.conclusion: The executing court’s order was not a decree because it did not adjudicate the claim. The High Court erred in dismissing the supervisory challenge on the basis that an appeal was required; its order was set aside and the matter was remitted for consideration under Article 227.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXI, Rules 97, 99 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an executing court must adjudicate relevant questions of right, title or interest raised by a person resisting dispossession or complaining of dispossession. Under Rules 98 and 100, an order made upon that adjudication is treated as a decree under Rule 103. A refusal to inquire into a claim on the ground of lack of jurisdiction, without adjudicating it, does not acquire that status. The Court relied on Noorduddin v. Dr. K.L. Anand, Babulal v. Raj Kumar, Ghasi Ram v. Chait Ram Saini, Bhanwar Lal v. Satyanarain, Brahmdeo Chaudhary v. Rishikesh Prasad Jaiswal, and S. Rajeswari v. S.N. Kulasekaran. It further applied Article 227 and the jurisdictional-error principles discussed in Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai, Joy Chand Lal Babu v. Kamalaksha Chaudhury, Keshardeo Chamria v. Radha Kissan Chamria, and Chaube Jagdish Prasad v. Ganga Prasad Chaturvedi.

predicates.third_party_execution_claim: A person other than the judgment-debtor raises a claim concerning an interest in property in execution proceedings.
predicates.court_refuses_inquiry_for_lack_of_jurisd: The executing court declines to inquire into the claim because it considers itself to lack jurisdiction.
predicates.court_does_not_decide_claim_merits: The executing court does not determine the claimant’s rights on the merits.

issues.definition: When a third party raises a claim in execution and the court refuses to inquire into it for want of jurisdiction without deciding its merits, the order is not treated as a decree.
